verdict.summary: A multi-tenant agent that reads Gmail through its backend needs an External consent screen, a Web application OAuth client, restricted-scope verification, and a CASA security assessment. Choose gmail.send if the product genuinely only sends mail: it is Sensitive rather than Restricted and has a stated 10-business-day verification estimate; a hosted read/metadata/modify agent follows the restricted path, estimated at six weeks for verification plus assessment. General-AI training or cross-user learning from Gmail data is prohibited.
verdict.activeEffort: 1–3 days, mostly building compliant consent assets, least-privilege justifications, a reviewer-accessible demo, and data-handling controls; the independent security assessment adds external coordination.
verdict.waitTime: Several weeks; Google estimates 6 weeks for restricted-scope verification plus security assessment, while a developer reported no first email after 3+ weeks (official and community-reported).
verdict.mainGate: Restricted Gmail scopes used through the agent's third-party backend require OAuth restricted-scope verification and a CASA security assessment.

recommendation.text: Use an External Google Auth Platform audience and a Web application OAuth client with server-side authorization-code flow. Start with gmail.send only if the visible user feature only sends messages; otherwise request the narrowest restricted scope required and budget for CASA because the hosted agent receives Gmail data.

essentials.text: Use authorization code flow; request access_type=offline on the initial authorization request, encrypt refresh tokens at rest, calculate access-token expiry from expires_in, and send the user through consent again when refresh fails. Refresh tokens can be invalidated or expire; use prompt=consent when a new token is needed while an old grant exists.

sources.quote: This value instructs the Google authorization server to return a refresh token and an access token the first time that your application exchanges an authorization code for tokens.
expires_in The remaining lifetime of the access token in seconds.
Never transmit tokens in plaintext, and always store encrypted tokens at rest
the user must revoke the existing grant or you must use the prompt=consent parameter in the initial authorization request

steps.title: Create the production Cloud project and set External audience

detail.text: Create or select the production Google Cloud project, then open Google Auth Platform > Branding and Audience and select External. Enter accurate app branding and current project owner/editor contacts so all-user authorization and review communications are possible.

sources.quote: In the Google API Console, go to Menu menu  > Google Auth platform  > Branding .
Projects configured with a user type of External are available to any user with a Google Account.
All communications with the OAuth review team will occur over email to the project owners and project editors configured when setting up your project.

detail.text: Publish a functional homepage and privacy policy on your owned domain; describe the agent's Gmail feature and disclose its Google-user-data access, use, storage, sharing, retention, and any human-review practice. Add and verify every domain used by the homepage, policy, redirect URI, and JavaScript origin.

sources.quote: The homepage must be hosted on a verified domain you own
The Privacy Policy should be hosted within the domain that hosts your homepage
Verify ownership of every domain associated with the home page, privacy policy, terms of service, redirect URIs, or JavaScript origins.

steps.title: Create the Web OAuth client and configure callback

detail.text: In the Cloud/API Console, open Credentials, create an OAuth client ID of type Web application, and add the exact production HTTPS callback URI on your verified domain. Do not include development-only redirects in this production client.

sources.quote: Click New Credentials , then select OAuth client ID .
The value must exactly match one of the authorized redirect URIs for the OAuth 2.0 client
Google OAuth clients used in production must not contain test environments, redirect URIs, or JavaScript origins available to only you or your development team.

steps.title: Select and declare minimal Gmail scopes

detail.text: In Google Auth Platform > Data Access, declare only the Gmail scopes used in production. Choose gmail.send for a send-only feature; use a restricted read, metadata, compose, or modify scope only when the user-visible feature cannot function with a narrower scope.

sources.quote: For example, for an app that only uses Gmail APIs to occasionally send emails on a user's behalf, don't request the scope that provides full access to the user's email data.
Enter all scopes your production app uses in its OAuth Consent Screen configuration.

steps.title: Produce callback validation checklist

detail.text: Use this checklist when entering the authorized redirect URI and implementing the callback so the OAuth request matches the registered production Web client.

sources.quote: Note that the http or https scheme, case, and trailing slash (' / ') must all match.
A developer must not direct a Google OAuth 2.0 authorization request to an embedded user-agent under the developer's control.

steps.output:
Callback checklist:
- Use one production HTTPS URI on an owned, verified domain.
- Copy it exactly into Credentials > Web application.
- Match scheme, host, path, case, and trailing slash in redirect_uri.
- Keep dev/staging redirects in separate projects.
- Do not use an embedded webview for Google authorization.
- Validate state on return before exchanging the code.

detail.text: Implement browser authorization against Google's HTTPS authorization endpoint with response_type=code, the selected scopes, state, exact redirect_uri, and access_type=offline; exchange the returned code server-side at the token endpoint, encrypt tokens, and refresh or re-consent on failure.

sources.quote: Google's OAuth 2.0 endpoint is at https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth . This endpoint is accessible only over HTTPS.
Set the parameter value to code for web server applications.
To exchange an authorization code for an access token, call the https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token endpoint

steps.title: Test with listed accounts and expiration handling

detail.text: Add controlled accounts as test users in the External consent screen, test connection, least-privilege Gmail actions, revocation, and reconnect behavior. Treat test-user authorization and offline refresh tokens as expiring seven days after consent.

sources.quote: Projects configured with a publishing status of Testing are limited to up to 100 test users listed in the OAuth consent screen.
If your OAuth client requests an offline access type and receives a refresh token, that token will also expire.

detail.text: Limit Gmail data use to a prominent user-facing productivity feature, obtain and document explicit consent before human inspection of specific messages, avoid advertising use and permanent copies, and prevent Gmail data from training or improving any shared AI model.

sources.quote: Applications that enhance the email experience for productivity purposes (such as applications for customer relationship management, delayed sending of email or mail merge, or providing generative AI summaries)
Transferring, selling, or using user data to create, train, or improve a machine learning or artificial intelligence model beyond that specific user’s personalized model
You have obtained and documented the user's explicit consent or affirmative agreement to view specific messages, files, or other data

steps.title: Prepare scope justification and reviewer script

detail.text: Adapt this script to the selected scope and record a reviewer-accessible video that demonstrates the submitted application, authorization flow, and actual scope use.

sources.quote: Provide a video that demonstrates the functionality, the OAuth flow of the app and shows how the scopes are being used.
Must show the same application you have submitted for verification (including app name, branding)

steps.output:
Reviewer script:
1. Show the public homepage, privacy policy, and matching app name.
2. Sign in as the supplied test user and click Connect Gmail.
3. Show the Google consent screen and each requested scope.
4. Demonstrate one visible feature using only those scopes.
5. Show disconnect/token deletion behavior.
6. Explain why a narrower scope cannot deliver this feature.
7. Confirm Gmail data is not used for shared-model training or ads.
